mixins_cold.program:
left = Module.new
middle = Module.new
right = Module.new
20_000.times do
  Class.new do
    include left
    prepend middle
    extend right
  end
end
puts :done

mixins_after_backing.program:
backing = Class.new(Module).new
Class.new { include backing }
left = Module.new
middle = Module.new
right = Module.new
20_000.times do
  Class.new do
    include left
    prepend middle
    extend right
  end
end
puts :done

method_identity.program:
left = Object.new
right = Object.new
200_000.times { left == right; left != right }
puts :done

performance_scope: The no-backing workload has no Module-subclass object and takes the original singleton hook lookup, guarded by one integer slot. Its reviewed +0.9% instruction increase is removed in the current-main comparison.

Once a Module-subclass backing exists, the flag stays set and the dispatch must distinguish its original Ruby receiver from an ordinary module. The warm ordinary-mixin workload exposes the residual lookup cost explicitly. Dropping this check would bypass subclass hooks; the optimization does not claim to remove this cost.

The cold and warm mixin workloads each create 20,000 classes and perform include, prepend and extend inside each class body. Three before/after pairs alternate order. Instructions include complete process startup.
